verses.1: So what should we do? We must cling to our sins, so that the grace of God may be increased.
verses.2: May it not happen! After all, we have died in sin. How can we still live in it?
verses.3: Do you not know that those who were baptized in Christ Jesus, they also baptized themselves into death?
verses.4: Thus, we were united with Him through baptism for death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead by the glory of His Father, so too we may walk in newness of life.
verses.5: For if we are united in the same nature of death, then we will also be united in the same nature of resurrection.
verses.6: Knowing this, we realize that our ancient man was crucified, so that his body might destroy the power of sin. He no longer had to serve us in sin.
verses.7: For when he dies, he is condemned due to his sin.
verses.8: And if we die with Christ, then we believe that we will also be united with Him.
verses.9: Since you know that Christ, who rose from the dead, will no longer die, death has no power over Him anymore.
verses.10: For he who died died because of his sins; but he who lives lives for God.
verses.11: Therefore, you also consider yourselves dead in your sins. But in Christ Jesus, you shall live for God.
verses.12: Therefore, do not let the sin of your mortal body lead you to obey its desires.
verses.13: Do not present your members as weapons of injustice against sin; instead, present yourselves to God as those who are living from the dead, and let your members be weapons of righteousness before God.
verses.14: For your sins will not be punished by law; they are not under the law, but rather by grace.
verses.15: So, have we sinned because we are not under law, but rather under grace? It didn’t happen like that.
verses.16: Don’t you know that the ones you present as slaves are actually slaves to whom you obey. So, are they sinners who deserve death, or are they those who deserve justice?
verses.17: But in the Lord’s eyes, it was right that you served as slaves of sin. Yet, from your hearts, you willingly gave yourself to Him in a manner that showed your willingness to learn from Him.
verses.18: But having been freed from sin, you were set free to serve justice.
verses.19: I say “human” because of the disease of your flesh. For just as you brought your limbs into servitude through impurity and sin, so too now you have brought your limbs into service for righteousness, for sanctification.
verses.20: For whether they were slaves of sin or free in justice.
verses.21: So, what kind of “fruit” did you have back then, that you now have to suffer from? After all, their ultimate fate was death.
verses.22: Now, having been freed from sin and becoming servants of God, you have received the reward for your efforts—holiness. The ultimate reward, however, is eternal life.
verses.23: For the consequences of sin are death; but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus, our Lord.
